issues.description: The `service` field on the frame complects a value (the request) with an identity (a live FrameProcessor reference).
issues.detail: A control frame is a value travelling through a pipeline; stuffing a mutable FrameProcessor object into it braids value and identity. Equality becomes object identity, the frame can never be serialized, logged faithfully, or replayed, and downstream code now holds a reference to a processor it has no business touching. A stable service name or id (data) would carry the same routing intent without the entanglement.

issues.description: Routing logic is complected across the switcher and every service that handles the frame.
issues.detail: The switcher decides whether to consume the frame by comparing `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service`, but the STT service and mock also re-push it unconditionally. The 'who consumes this' contract is now split between two places that must agree. A single decomposed rule — switcher consumes when target matches, services always forward — would be one concept in one place.

issues.description: Targeting non-active services is silently undefined behavior rather than explicit data.
issues.detail: `push_frame` only suppresses the frame when `frame.service == active_service`. If a frame targets an inactive service (a perfectly reasonable future case), it escapes the switcher and leaks downstream. The time semantics — 'who is active when this frame arrives' — are never made explicit. Either forbid non-active targets in the type, or handle both branches as named cases.

issues.description: Renaming `RequestMetadataFrame` to `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` couples the frame's name to one caller.
issues.detail: The frame is a generic request: 're-emit your metadata.' Naming it after the switcher binds a value-shaped concept to one identity that happens to send it today. If another component ever needs the same request, the name lies. `RequestServiceMetadataFrame` would describe the value; the switcher prefix describes who sends it, which is incidental.

issues.description: The question that should have been asked first: why does metadata need a pull request at all?
issues.detail: Metadata is a value about a service at a moment. If services published their current metadata value (and switches were observable), downstream processors could read it without a round-trip control frame. The current design — switch, then ask the new service to re-announce — exists because metadata is treated as an event rather than a queryable value. Worth a hammock pass before extending the request protocol further.

review.summary: The rename is fine; the new `service: FrameProcessor` field is where the design takes on incidental complexity. A control frame is a value, and embedding a live processor reference complects value with identity, makes the frame unserializable, and splits the 'who consumes this' decision between the switcher and every service that handles it. The target-mismatch case is silently undefined. None of this is essential — a service id (data) plus a single consume rule in the switcher would be SIMPLE; the current shape is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE because it reuses the object reference already in hand. Worth one hammock pass on whether metadata should be a pulled event or a published value before extending this protocol further.
